answer.rationale: Memory 57 is strongest because it explicitly reports qualified revenue and no measurable retention harm, both central to sustainable long-term revenue. Memory 44 has strong pipeline-quality relevance but omits closed-won revenue, retention, and sales-cost evidence. Memories 31, 86, and 91 show early activation, adoption, or engagement improvements, which are useful leading indicators but do not establish qualified revenue, monetization, or durability. Memory 73 reports acquisition and revenue lift in the relevant price-sensitive SMB segment, but targeted discounting leaves margin, retention, and long-run price-positioning unaddressed. Memory 86 is least supported because improved onboarding completion and time-to-value are especially indirect proxies for the stated revenue objective and omit both revenue and retention outcomes.
